Subject: Pricing exhibit clarifications and redlines (Exhibit B)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — TidePoint procurement reviewed the draft order form and we have a couple of substantive asks in Exhibit B (pricing schedule) before legal will sign. I attached our redline (TidePoint_Redline_ExhibitB.pdf) and a marked Word for convenience. High-level asks: 

- Pro-rata true-up: If usage for a calendar month is partial (customer onboarding mid-month or deletion of workloads mid-billing cycle), we need the calculation spelled out (we prefer daily pro-ration based on calendar days, not token buckets). Please confirm language and an example calculation.
- Minimum monthly commit / floor: we want a soft floor that allows true-up at quarter-end instead of immediately billing shortfalls every month — can that be accommodated?
- Caps & surcharge: the redline proposes a soft cap on overage surcharge to protect smaller spikes; we need Redwood to confirm operational impact.
- Effective date & retroactivity: we asked that the pricing schedule only take effect on the execution date and not retroactively by usage start.

Can you route to your legal/ops and propose specific text for Exhibit B (we flagged the lines in the PDF)? Also please confirm whether your billing system can emit a daily usage export so our finance team can reconcile if we accept calendar-day pro-ration.

Goal: confirm wording and get a final Order Form v3 we can route to our CFO and DocuSign by next week.

Best,

Hi Amy — thanks for the clear notes and the redlines, appreciate the markup. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (account lead) to propose precise Exhibit B wording and confirm billing feasibility. A couple quick clarifications from ops before we draft language: 

1) When you say "calendar-day pro-ration," do you want pro-ration strictly by calendar days (e.g., Oct 1–15 = 15/31) or by hours? Our platform currently calculates by calendar days when customers request it, so calendar days is fine operationally.
2) For the "soft floor" (monthly minimum true-up at quarter-end) — do you want a binding quarterly true-up (i.e., no invoice for shortfalls until quarter close) or a billing credit that appears monthly but is reconciled quarterly? That affects revenue recognition and internal process.

We should be able to provide a daily usage export (CSV) via the console API for reconciliation; I'll ask ops to confirm the field list (date, token_count, model_id, route).

Laura and Karthik — can you propose Exhibit B language that: (a) defines pro-ration by calendar days, (b) offers an optional quarterly true-up flow (customer elects quarterly true-up at signature), and (c) caps overage surcharge to X% with a carve-out for burst events? Amy — if you're ok, we'll draft both a conservative legal version and a finance-friendly variant so TidePoint can choose.

Hi all — reviewed TidePoint's redline and Markus's questions. Below is proposed replacement text for the relevant sections of Exhibit B. We kept the language concise and added an example calculation; Amy, please confirm the math and whether the quarterly option meets your procurement requirement.

--- PROPOSED EXHIBIT B LANGUAGE (pricing schedule) ---
1. Pro-Ration. For any partial billing period, charges will be prorated on a calendar-day basis. Example: if the Service is activated on October 11 and the calendar month has 31 days, Customer is billed (21/31) of the monthly committed amount for October.

2. True-Up Option. Customer may elect, at signature, one of the following true-up methods by indicating the election on the Order Form: 
  a) Monthly True-Up: invoiced monthly for any shortfall between actual usage and committed minimums; or
  b) Quarterly True-Up (Optional): invoiced at the end of each calendar quarter for aggregate shortfalls across the quarter; no monthly shortfall invoices will be issued under this election.

3. Overage Cap. Overage rates apply to usage above committed volumes. Except for documented burst events (defined as any 24-hour window where usage exceeds 3x the historical 30-day average and is reported to Redwood within 5 business days), Customer's overage surcharge will not exceed 50% of the per-unit list price in effect on the Invoice Date.

4. Effective Date. Pricing in this Exhibit applies to usage occurring on or after the Effective Date specified on the Order Form. No retrospective pricing adjustments will be applied to usage prior to the Effective Date.

5. Reconciliation Export. Upon request, Redwood will provide a machine-readable usage export (CSV) with daily granularity including date, token_count, model_id, and route for reconciliation purposes.

--- END PROPOSED LANGUAGE ---

Notes on impact: 
- Finance: Quarterly True-Up delays revenue recognition of shortfalls by up to 60 days; if TidePoint chooses that option we will align invoicing cadence accordingly.
- Ops: calendar-day pro-ration + CSV export are feasible; we will surface the export field list and sample within 48 business hours once you confirm.

If TidePoint accepts the language except for the overage cap percentage, propose a target cap and we can run a quick impact estimate. Karthik/Marissa: once Amy confirms, please prepare a final Order Form v3 with the Exhibit B insert and a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
